newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Poor in Albania sell blood to survive.
newsitem.headline: Poor in Albania sell blood to survive.

text.p: Scores of impoverished Albanians, who lost the few savings they had in collapsed pyramid schemes, are queuing up each day in medical centres to sell their blood for cash.

Newspapers report a surge in blood selling since a variety of pyramid investment schemes began to go under, leaving savers with little money to pay for food and other basics in a country lacking a proper welfare system.
"We have three people in the family and we have no money," Nexhmie Myfteri, 38, told Reuters at Tirana's blood centre on the outskirts of the capital.
"This is our only source of income," she said.
Donors can earn 2,500 leks ($22) for giving 400 millilitres of blood and at least 30 to 40 people a day visit the centre to receive the payment.
Some 10 adults were seen on Thursday morning lying on reclining chairs next to nurses wearing rubber gloves who syringed blood out of their arms.
Alban Nurce, 23, who has two small children, said he had lost $3,000 in one collapsed pyramid scheme.
"I have two children and no money for bread," he said.
After giving the blood, donors queue up again at a counter where cash in local currency is handed out. ($1=114 Lek)
